tt-7673230653814623502.caption: Korean Japgokbap (잡곡밥) — Multigrain Rice An easy way to add more whole grains, fiber, and texture to your rice—and perfect for meal prepping! 💛 🌾 You’ll need: • 1 cup @Kim'C Market Organic 5 Colored Rice (Use link in bio under My Favorites or use code BUSYMAMAEASYBITES for $10 off)  • 2 cups short or medium-grain white rice • Filtered water Wash the 5 colored rice about 3 times, then soak for 30 minutes to help soften the outer layer of the grains. Add the white rice and wash everything together 3–4 more times, until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer to your rice cooker and add filtered water. I use the Korean hand method—place your hand flat over the rice and add water up to the knuckles where your fingers meet your palm. Cook on the multigrain setting (mine takes about 45 minutes), until the grains are tender. Fluff and mix! 🍚 To freeze: Scoop into ½-cup portions—I use a muffin tray—and freeze for a few hours before transferring to a labeled freezer bag. To reheat: Place a portion in a bowl, sprinkle with a little water, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave until piping hot all the way through.  Such an easy staple to have ready for busy nights! 🙌🏼 #Easyrecipe #Freezerprep #Mealprep #Koreanfood #koreanfoodlovers☺️🍶🍲🍜🍣

tt-7674995086555417870.caption: 🫐 2-Ingredient Blueberry Chia Jam for Toddlers 💙 So simple, naturally sweet, and perfect to keep on hand for PB&Js, toast, oatmeal, yogurt, pancakes, and more! Ingredients: • 1 cup fresh or frozen blueberries • 1 tbsp chia seeds • Optional sweetener — I skip it when the berries are nice and sweet! How to make it: Add the blueberries to a small saucepan and cook over low-medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until they burst and become soft and juicy. Gently mash them to your preferred texture. Turn off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp chia seeds, and let the jam sit for a few minutes. The chia seeds will soften and gel as the mixture cools, giving you that perfect jammy texture. 🫐 Store some in an airtight container in the fridge for the week, then freeze the rest in single-serve portions. I love having little portions ready to thaw whenever we want a quick PB&J. 🙌 #ToddlerRecipes #ToddlerMeals #ToddlerFood #easyrecipe #jam

tt-7675566140340391181.caption: Easy Toddler Blueberry Muffins 🍌🫐 Makes: about 12 mini muffins or 6 regular muffins Ingredients * 1 ripe banana, mashed * 1 egg * ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt  * 2 tablespoons melted butter or neutral oil * 1 teaspoon vanilla extract  * ¾ cup all-purpose flour * ½ teaspoon baking soda * ½ cup blueberries, fresh or frozen Directions 1. Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a mini muffin pan or use liners. 2. Mash the banana well. Stir in the egg, yogurt, melted butter, and vanilla. 3. Add flour and baking soda. Stir just until combined. 4. Gently fold in the blueberries. For younger toddlers, you can smush or chop larger blueberries. 5. Fill muffin cups. 6. Bake ~15 minutes for mini muffins or ~20-30 minutes for regular muffins, until a toothpick comes out clean. 7. Cool before serving.  #easyrecipe #toddlermeals #momrecipes❤️ #toddlerbreakfast #toddlersnack

tt-7676197216297553165.caption: #Ad  Would you put an entire avocado into chocolate muffins? 🥑🍫 Research has shown that as kids get older, they tend to eat fewer fruits and vegetables. Fresh avocados are one simple and delicious way to include more fruit in back-to-school meals and snacks.  Today I’m partnering with @aguacatesloveonetoday to make these Avocado Chocolate Muffins have become one of my favorite make-ahead snacks for busy school weeks. Fresh avocados are the star of this recipe, creating an incredibly soft, rich texture while contributing healthy unsaturated fats, fiber and more than 20 vitamins and minerals. Recipe Ingredients ● 1 ripe avocado ● ½ cup all purpose flour or oat flour ● 2 eggs ● ⅓ cup peanut butter ● ⅓ cup maple syrup ● ⅓ cup cocoa powder ● 1 tsp vanilla extract ● 1 tsp baking powder ● Handful of chocolate chips Directions 1. If using oat flour, blend the oats into a fine flour. 2. Add the avocado and all remaining ingredients except the chocolate chips, then blend until smooth. 3. Fold in the chocolate chips. 4. Pour into a greased muffin tin. 5. Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes. 6. Let cool completely before serving. Have you ever baked with avocado before? @Aguacates - Love One Today #loveonetoday

tt-7680031735425305869.caption: Toddler Breakfast Bites ✈️🍳 These were SO simple to make and honestly aren’t just for toddlers — they’re an easy breakfast for the whole family! I enjoy them too, which makes them perfect for meal prep when you don’t want to make separate breakfasts for everyone. We have an upcoming flight, and I’m planning to pack these for my toddler so we have something homemade, filling, and easy to eat instead of having to grab airport food. ✈️ Ingredients: ✨ 1 cup ground chicken 🥕 Optional: finely chopped carrots + mushrooms 🥚 3 eggs — 2 scrambled + 1 raw for binding 🧀 ¼ cup cottage cheese 🧀 ¼ cup shredded cheese 🥄 2 tbsp all-purpose flour My ground chicken already had finely chopped carrots and mushrooms mixed in from another meal, so I used that! You can totally leave the veggies out or add whatever finely chopped veggies you have on hand. How to make: Cook the ground chicken until fully cooked (along with the veggies if using). Scramble 2 eggs separately. Let everything cool slightly, then combine with 1 raw egg, cottage cheese, shredded cheese, and flour. Form into little bites/patties and bake at 350°F convection for 25 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the centers reach 165°F. Let them cool and enjoy! 🤍 Make a batch for the whole family or save them for an easy grab-and-go breakfast. Save this for your next busy morning or travel day! ✈️ #toddlerbreakfast #toddlerrecipes #toddlermeals #familybreakfast #easyrecipe

video.narration: Hi, I'm tb and today was round 2 of IVF making a baby now involves needles and a small pharmacy in my fridge People get a little weird when I tell them we're going through IVF They get even weirder when I tell them I had three miscarriages and I get it People don't know what to say because they're terrified of saying the wrong thing grief is weird and everyone does it differently For me it was realizing my first child was an absolute miracle I just didn't know enough at the time. Another part was talking about what happened a lot and probably more than some people were prepared for But saying it out loud helped every time I told a story it felt less like a This terrible thing that happened to me and a little more like complaining about a delayed flight and kindness is what healed me Not perfectly chosen words. Maybe sharing everything was also my way of testing myself Can I say this out loud and still be okay? Can I say it without falling apart? Turns out yes, so I guess that's what grief looked like for me talking about it until the words stopped hurting and Letting a lot of very kind people say slightly awkward things

tt-7684065280766610701.caption: Toddler Korean Bulgogi Rice Balls 🇰🇷🍚✨ An easy Korean-inspired meal that my toddler can pick up and eat with her hands! These bulgogi rice balls are savory with a little natural sweetness from applesauce and come together so quickly. My toddler loves these, and they’re an easy way to get protein + veggies into one bite. 🤍 🥩 Ingredients: • 1 lb ground beef • ½ medium carrot, finely chopped • ½ medium onion, finely diced • 2 cloves garlic, minced • Finely diced mushrooms • 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce • 1 tbsp sesame oil • 2 tbsp unsweetened applesauce • Sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds • Cooked rice • Olive oil for cooking You can also add in any finely chopped veggies you have on hand! 🍳 How to make them: 1. Sauté the garlic and onion in a little olive oil until fragrant. 2. Add the carrots and cook until they begin to soften. 3. Add the ground beef and cook through, breaking it into small pieces. I used a paper towel to carefully dab away any excess fat. 4. Add the finely diced mushrooms or any other finely chopped veggies you’d like. 5. Stir in the low-sodium soy sauce, sesame oil and applesauce. 6. Continue cooking until everything is fully cooked and combined, then sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. 7. Mix the bulgogi beef with cooked rice. 8. Once cool enough to handle, use your hands to form into toddler-sized rice balls. That’s it! 🙌 Easy, quick, and perfect for little hands. My toddler loves being able to pick these up and feed herself! Save this one for an easy toddler lunch or dinner! 🫶 #toddlerrecipes #toddlermeals #toddlerfood #koreanfood #easyrecipe

tt-7691705534185098509.caption: The viral brothy beef bowl… but make it toddler-friendly 🤍 I made my own creamy version using @Kettle and Fire Beef Bone Broth and turned it into a dinner my toddler AND the rest of the family can enjoy. The broth is really what brings the whole bowl together 🙌 I used Kettle & Fire as the base to make it flavorful and comforting while keeping the recipe simple enough for a weeknight dinner. Save this one! 👇 Toddler-Friendly Creamy Brothy Beef Bowl Beef • 1 lb ground beef • 1 cup grated carrot • ½ tsp garlic powder • ½ tsp onion powder • ½ tsp paprika • Black pepper, optional Creamy broth • 2 cups  Beef Bone Broth • 1 tbsp tomato paste • 1 garlic clove, minced • ¼ cup heavy cream • ¼ cup finely shredded cheddar • ½ tsp Italian seasoning To serve: cooked rice + optional parsley How to make it: Brown the ground beef and grated carrot with the seasonings until cooked through and golden. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds, then add tomato paste and cook for 1–2 minutes. Pour in the Beef Bone Broth, add Italian seasoning, and simmer for 5 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in the heavy cream and cheddar until creamy. Add rice to your bowl, top with the beef, and ladle that creamy broth over everything. 🤍 For toddlers, I like adding enough broth to make the rice extra soft and saucy. For the adults, add cucumber, parsley, black pepper, or red pepper flakes. One dinner for the whole family 🙌 #kfpartner #toddlermeals #familydinner #toddlerrecipes #easyfamilymeals

ingredients: 1 medium apple, chopped (gala, fuji, or golden delicious)
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F.
Toast the bread cubes for 8-10 minutes to dry them out. Alternatively, you can use day old bread that is already dried out.
Increase oven temperature to 350°F.
Heat oil in a sauté pan. Add the sausage and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until slightly golden. Remove sausage to a large mixing bowl to cool.

In the same saute pan, add the butter and sauté the onions for 3 minutes. Add the celery, apples, and thyme and sauté for an additional 5 minutes, until everything is heated through and the veggies are tender. Allow to cool a few minutes before continuing.

Place the bread cubes, cooled sautéed vegetables and remaining ingredients into the large mixing bowl with the sausage and toss to thoroughly combine. (It's important that your ingredients are cool to the touch before adding the eggs so that they don't scramble.)
Spoon the stuffing mixture into greased muffin tins, filling all the way to the top. Pat the mixture down to pack it well.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the tops are just golden.

ingredients: 4 cups grated cheddar cheese (shred it yourself for best melting!)
1 pound elbow macaroni (you can also use campanelle, cavatappi, or shells)
steps: Place the topping ingredients in a bowl and stir to combine.
Preheat oven to 400° F.
Cook pasta in salted water* for about 3 minutes less than package directions call for, until al dente, reserving half a cup of the pasta water.
In a large pot melt the butter and then add the flour, whisking continuously over low-medium heat for 2-3 minutes to make a roux.
Slowly whisk in the milk and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, whisking occasionally, 3 to 4 minutes, or until sauce is gently bubbling and starting to thicken.
Add reserved pasta water and cheddar cheese and whisk until melted.
Stir in the pasta.
Transfer to a greased 9"x13" baking dish.
Sprinkle topping on macaroni and cheese.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until top is golden and bubbling.

ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into chunks
1/4 cup old fashioned oats (also known as 5 minute oats)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Place the first 6 ingredients in a food processor until chicken is finely chopped and ingredients are combined.
Place the bread crumbs and parmesan cheese in a shallow bowl or on a plate and stir to combine.
With moistened hands, roll 1 tablespoon of chicken mixture between your palms and flatten it into a “nugget” shape.
Gently press nuggets into bread crumbs to evenly coat them.
Place nuggets on parchment lined baking sheet and lightly spray nuggets with cooking spray.

Bake for 12-15 minutes or until golden and serve. If you want your nuggets to be more golden brown, place under the broiler for 2 minutes after cooking. Air frying instructions are in the notes below!

ingredients: 1/2 cup pure maple syrup, honey, or agave
2 1/4 cup rolled oats (gluten-free rolled oats if needed)
1 1/4 cup chocolate chips or chunks, divided (1 cup in batter and 1/4 cup for topping)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease 12 cup muffin tin (you can also place paper liners in muffins cups without greasing).
Place all the ingredients (except for the chocolate chips) in a blender, starting with the wet ingredients, followed by the dry.
Blend for 10 seconds or until oats begin to become fine (it's okay if there are some bigger oat pieces left). Add 1 cup chocolate chips then blend for another 10 seconds.
Using a quarter cup ice cream scoop or spoon, divide batter between 12 muffin cups filling 3/4 to the top.
Divide the remaining 1/4 cup chocolate chips on top of the muffins.
Bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.

ingredients: 1 pound rigatoni or favorite shaped pasta
1 pound large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined (I used frozen shrimp that I defrosted)
2 tablespoons parsley, chopped (+ more for sprinkling)
steps: In a large pot, bring 4 quarts of water plus 1 tbsp of salt to a boil.
Cook the pasta according to package directions and drain reserving 1 cup of the pasta water.
While pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saute pan over medium heat.
Place the shrimp, garlic and 1/4 tsp salt in a saute pan and cook for 3 minutes, stirring halfway through (make sure not to overcook the shrimp).
Remove the shrimp to a plate and add the clam juice into the same saute pan.
Bring the clam juice to a boil for 5 minutes or until the liquid is reduced by half.
Whisk the butter, lemon juice and parsley into the saute pan and add the pasta, shrimp and as much of the reserved pasta water as necessary to make a sauce to coat the pasta.
Top with additional parsley or grated cheese if desired.

2 red bell peppers, cut into large chunks
1 delicata squash, unpeeled, split lengthwise, seeds removed and cut into half moons
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Place all the vegetables on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat all the vegetables and sprinkle with salt. Alternatively at this point you can place the vegetables in a large zipper bag and refrigerate overnight.
Roast for 45-50 minutes, stirring halfway through, or until tender and golden.
Remove the vegetables from the oven, drizzle with maple syrup and roast an additional 5 minutes or until caramelized and golden.
Serve with additional salt to taste.

ingredients: 1 1/4 cups almond, oat, soy or other plant based milk of choice
1 tablespoon maple syrup, plus more for serving
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for greasing
steps: Mix the dry ingredients in a bowl.
Mix the wet ingredients in a separate bowl.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and whisk to combine (don’t over mix, some lumps are fine).
Heat a griddle or large saute pan over medium heat and lightly
grease with oil.
Ladle as many pancakes as possible (about 2 tbsp of batter for each one) on the griddle and cook 2 minutes or until bubbles start forming on the surface and the bottom is golden brown.
Flip the pancakes and cook another 2 minutes.
Repeat the process until you run out of batter (you can hold the finished pancakes in a 250 degree oven while you finish making the pancakes).
Serve with maple syrup and enjoy.
